item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-54d6b311a940a59a","start_unit":9,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"The World Bank diagnosed Mexico as having macroeconomic stability and resilient financial-sector institutions, while identifying stagnant productivity, persistent poverty, inequality, and regional disparities as major inherited challenges. The 2013-2018 National Development Plan set goals of peace, inclusion, education quality, prosperity, and responsible international engagement, with cross-cutting strategies for productivity, modern government, and gender.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.10","6B.1","6B.10","8B.1"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Pre-period baseline and stated inherited program context; not evidence of López Obrador's 2023 conduct or outcomes.","ruler_attribution":"The document concerns Mexico's 2013-2018 administration under President Enrique Peña Nieto, not Andrés Manuel López Obrador.","limitations":["No direct evidence about López Obrador or 2023.","The World Bank's diagnosis and NDP description are not an independent evaluation of later implementation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-54d6b311a940a59a","start_unit":21,"end_unit":22,"fact_summary":"The incoming administration in 2013 submitted or announced reforms in telecommunications, education, finance, public finance, and energy. The reforms included competition and information-access measures, teacher selection and evaluation, financial-sector oversight and consumer protection, progressive-tax and social-insurance proposals, and an energy-investment agenda. The National Development Plan was developed through broad public consultation and included targets and indicators.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.6","5B.1","5B.3","5B.4","5B.7","6B.2","6B.5","8B.1","8B.2"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Pre-period evidence of a prior administration's program design and consultation process; useful only as historical baseline for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Actions are attributed to President Enrique Peña Nieto's administration, not López Obrador.","limitations":["The source does not establish whether these reforms were sustained, reversed, or improved by 2023.","Several measures were proposals or announcements rather than demonstrated outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-54d6b311a940a59a","start_unit":27,"end_unit":29,"fact_summary":"The World Bank reported that Mexico had adopted an ambitious climate plan and General Climate Change Bill targeting a 30% CO2 reduction by 2020 and 50% by 2050 relative to 2000, but noted continuing high emissions, rising vehicle ownership, environmental degradation, and the need for stronger monitoring and public availability of environmental indicators.","question_ids":["1B.9","1B.10","5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","5B.10","6B.6","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Pre-period environmental baseline and inherited legal commitments; does not measure 2023 implementation.","ruler_attribution":"The commitments described were adopted before López Obrador's presidency and are not attributed to him.","limitations":["No 2023 emissions, enforcement, budget, or correction evidence.","Climate and environmental outcomes have long causal lags and substantial external influences."]},{"source_id":"SRC-54d6b311a940a59a","start_unit":31,"end_unit":34,"fact_summary":"The prior National Development Plan identified drug-trafficking-linked criminal activity, violence against women and children, and public perceptions of slow and sometimes corrupt judicial and police institutions as security challenges. It proposed youth education and employment, violence-prevention policies, and promotion of a more humane, agile, efficient, and accessible justice system.","question_ids":["2B.10","3B.1","3B.2","3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","8B.1","8B.2"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Inherited pre-2023 domestic-safety baseline and prior policy program; not evidence of López Obrador's implementation.","ruler_attribution":"The diagnosis and proposed interventions belong to the Peña Nieto administration's NDP.","limitations":["The document does not provide 2023 violence, enforcement, accountability, or outcome data.","It does not establish whether proposed measures were implemented or effective."]},{"source_id":"SRC-54d6b311a940a59a","start_unit":58,"end_unit":61,"fact_summary":"The World Bank reported that Mexico's public-finance modernization initiatives included results-based management, performance-informed budgeting, a government financial-management information system, and evaluation functions, but said these required institutionalization and better outcome information. Procurement reform remained important because procurement represented about 40% of the federal budget and carried substantial waste and corruption risks.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","7B.6","7B.9","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Pre-period institutional baseline relevant to inherited administrative capacity; no direct 2023 assessment.","ruler_attribution":"The described reforms and institutional conditions predate López Obrador and are not attributed to him.","limitations":["No evidence of López Obrador's appointments, procurement decisions, audits, or corrective actions.","The source is a policy diagnosis and does not independently verify all implementation claims."]},{"source_id":"SRC-54d6b311a940a59a","start_unit":60,"end_unit":63,"fact_summary":"The World Bank's completion assessment rated the prior country program broadly satisfactory, but recorded mixed results: fiscal policy was partially achieved; financial-sector reform, employment support, trade-cost reduction, education, social inclusion, urban transport, and environmental outcomes were often achieved; innovation, health-system capacity, housing, energy access, and institutional outcomes were partly achieved; customs-process reform was not achieved.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.7","5B.10","6B.2","6B.5","6B.10","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Historical evaluation of FY2008-2013, useful for baseline and implementation-capacity context but not for 2023 scoring.","ruler_attribution":"The evaluation concerns the Calderón administration and World Bank program, not López Obrador.","limitations":["The assessment is partly a World Bank self-evaluation and may reflect institutional reporting incentives.","It does not evaluate López Obrador's period."]},{"source_id":"SRC-54d6b311a940a59a","start_unit":65,"end_unit":66,"fact_summary":"During the 2008-2013 period, Mexico's Oportunidades program reached 5.8 million families and expanded children's participation; Popular Health Insurance grew from 27 million to more than 52 million affiliates; early-childhood-development attendance increased; and influenza surveillance, vaccination, antiviral reserves, and risk communication were strengthened, although the influenza loan was cancelled and the health-system outcome was only partially achieved.","question_ids":["3B.9","3B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.6","6B.9","6B.10","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Historical social-policy and emergency-preparedness baseline; not evidence about López Obrador's 2023 decisions.","ruler_attribution":"Results are attributed to earlier administrations and programs, with World Bank support.","limitations":["Reported outcomes precede 2023 and cannot establish continuity or causal attribution to López Obrador.","The document notes both achieved outputs and incomplete health-system strengthening."]},{"source_id":"SRC-54d6b311a940a59a","start_unit":71,"end_unit":74,"fact_summary":"The prior program expanded public access-to-information infrastructure: INFOMEX became operational in all 31 states and several autonomous entities, while a public municipal-management observatory and budget-performance portal supported information sharing and accountability. However, the Congressional monitoring and evaluation system was not achieved, and judicial modernization reached only five of ten targeted applications.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.4","4B.6","4B.10","5B.7","7B.6","7B.7","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Pre-2023 institutional baseline; no direct evidence of López Obrador's treatment of transparency, courts, Congress, or information access.","ruler_attribution":"These developments concern the prior administration and World Bank-supported projects.","limitations":["The source does not assess later deterioration, preservation, or expansion of these systems.","It provides project-level results rather than ruler-level accountability evidence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-54d6b311a940a59a","start_unit":109,"end_unit":110,"fact_summary":"The World Bank's reform diagnosis found that Mexico's economy had grown at less than 2% annually over the preceding decade, with per-capita income around 30% of the U.S. level, and attributed weak productivity to financial, regulatory, labor-market, skills, innovation, and competition constraints. It also identified persistent poverty, inequality, regional disparities, and weak labor-income gains as central challenges.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.4","5B.8","5B.10","6B.3","6B.10","8B.1","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Pre-2023 inherited economic baseline; not a 2023 outcome assessment.","ruler_attribution":"The diagnosis predates López Obrador and is not attributed to him.","limitations":["No evidence of policies or outcomes under López Obrador.","The analysis identifies plausible constraints but does not establish their relative causal weight."]},{"source_id":"SRC-54d6b311a940a59a","start_unit":118,"end_unit":122,"fact_summary":"The World Bank reported persistent poverty and vulnerability, large regional disparities, gender and indigenous disadvantages, a fragmented social-protection system, regressive energy subsidies, coverage gaps for informal workers and older people, and limited protection against economic shocks. It also noted that Oportunidades and Seguro Popular were successful programs but insufficient as a fully integrated system.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.7","6B.8","6B.9","6B.10","8B.1","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Pre-2023 baseline of inherited welfare and distributional conditions; not evidence of López Obrador's 2023 performance.","ruler_attribution":"The conditions and programs described predate López Obrador's administration.","limitations":["No 2023 incidence, eligibility, service-quality, or correction evidence.","National averages and program coverage do not establish equitable access or actual welfare improvement."]},{"source_id":"SRC-54d6b311a940a59a","start_unit":127,"end_unit":130,"fact_summary":"The World Bank described progress toward performance-informed budgeting, financial-management systems, and evaluation, but emphasized that institutionalization, quality outcome data, accounting harmonization, procurement oversight, and stronger federal-subnational capacity remained necessary. It also reported low tax collection, heavy dependence of subnational governments on federal transfers, and persistent fiscal-discipline problems in some states.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10","7B.6","7B.7","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Historical baseline for fiscal and administrative capacity; not evidence of 2023 conduct.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern Mexico before López Obrador's term.","limitations":["No direct evidence about 2023 budget execution, audits, appointments, or corrective action.","The document offers recommendations and diagnosis alongside partial implementation evidence."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied source is a 2013 World Bank country-strategy document covering FY2014-2019 and earlier historical data; it contains no direct evidence about Andrés Manuel López Obrador's conduct, decisions, or outcomes in 2023.","Facts are therefore limited to inherited baselines, prior institutional conditions, and pre-2023 programs; no scoring inference is made.","The source is one document, fully accounted for above."]}
